messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I'm experimenting with a preseed traffic mixer for deploy-time warmers to improve KV prefix hit-rate. Posting notes and a short experiment plan.
Mira: Nice. Quick numbers from baseline?
Alex: Baseline after a canary deploy: prefix hit-rate ~18% at t+5m, tail latency spikes at 95th. Goal: push hit-rate to ~40–50% within first 10m without adding too much cost.
Jordan: What's the mixer pattern? synthetic vs live sampling?
Alex: Hybrid. Mixer composes three streams:
  1) recent live prefixes (5m sliding window, sampled by weight)
  2) synthetic long-tail prefixes generated from corpus (to cover cold keys)
  3) deterministic replay of top-200 routes for immediate coverage
Alex: Early profiling shows interaction with kernel selection/batching: after the fused-attn kernel swap, our continuous-batching window effectively shrank (merge rate dropped), so warmers that relied on large merge windows to upsweep KV cache aren't creating as many KV fills.
Mira: So regression caused by kernel switch -> less batching -> fewer prefetches -> lower hit-rate. Can we tweak batching heuristics instead of reverting kernel?
Alex: Yes. Two levers we can try in parallel:
  - increase warmers RPS for the first 3m (cheap synthetic traffic burst)
  - bump batching.window_ms from 8 -> 12 for warmers-only traffic class
Sam: Any risk to latency if we increase batching.window_ms?
Alex: Slight increase in tail for warmed requests, but overall the warmed requests are served from cache so net tail improves. Unwarmed traffic could see small added ms. Plan: scope change to the preseed traffic route via routing policy.
Leo: Can you share the CronJob we used for scheduled warmers? want to replicate.
Alex: Pasted below — simple k8s CronJob that fires the mixer every 2m during deploy window.

```
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: preseed-mixer
spec:
  schedule: "*/2 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: mixer
            image: redwood/warmers:canary
            args: ["--duration=60","--rps=40","--mode=hybrid"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

Jordan: Nice. What's the synthetic generator config? We don't want high-entropy keys that pollute cache.
Alex: Generator uses prefix-weighted sampling with entropy cap: we fold long tail to max cardinality per route. Config snippet:

```
{"mode":"prefix_weighted","max_cardinality":5000,"tail_smooth_factor":0.6}
```

Mira: How are we measuring success?
Alex: Metrics:
  - prefix_hit_rate (global + per-route) at t+1/5/10m
  - kv_population_rate (unique keys/sec) during warmers
  - 95p latency delta vs baseline
  - cost estimate (tokens generated)

Alex: Quick early result from an internal canary: hit-rate went 18% -> 44% at t+5m with mixer rps=40, batching.window_ms=12 for warmers-only.
Sam: Logs?
Alex: small excerpt from canary:

```
2026-03-01T12:05:34Z CACHE_EVENT prefix=checkout:user:123 hit=false populate=true latency=3ms
2026-03-01T12:05:34Z PREFETCH prefix=checkout:user:123 kv_put=true size=32 latency=1ms
2026-03-01T12:05:35Z CACHE_EVENT prefix=checkout:user:123 hit=true latency=0.8ms
```

Leo: Deploy-bot pinged the canary deploy? @deploy-bot
deploy-bot: canary-deploy #2314 completed — routing updated
Mira: Two quick follow-ups:
  1) Can we add a short-lived TTL tag to synthetic keys so they don't persist in long-term KV? (avoid cache pollution)
  2) Add regression guard: if global 95p latency increases >5% rollback the batching.window change
Alex: Agreed on both. Implemented TTL via header x-warm-ttl=300s in mixer. Added rollback rule to rollout pipeline.
Jordan: Experiment proposal steps?
Alex: Short plan
  - A: rollout mixer to 5% traffic on canary; run for 15m; collect metrics
  - B: if hit-rate >= 35% and 95p latency delta <= +3% -> expand to 25%
  - C: at 25% observe 30m; if stable, promote change to 100% for warmers route

Sam: Any other perf surprises we've seen with kernel selection?
Alex: Aside from batching window effect, we saw a small regression in KV write throughput due to concurrent IO scheduling on the newer kernel path. Mitigation: cap concurrent prefetch workers per GPU (config: prefetch.max_workers=6) — helps smoothing.
Leo: Sounds good. Can I get the quick commands to trigger a mixer run for testing?
Alex: Sure. One-off trigger:

```
curl -X POST https://internal.api.redwood/preseed/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"mode":"hybrid","duration":60,"rps":60}'
```

Mira: I'll run this on the next canary and post metrics here.
Sam: :thumbsup:
Jordan: Also can we add a micro-benchmark for kernel changes that measures effective batch-merge rate? would help catch regressions automatically.
Alex: Good idea — adding perf job to CI that emits merge_rate, avg_batch_size, kv_prefill_rate.
Mira: Thanks — will coordinate the rollout with SRE for the autoscale window (we don't want warmers to accidentally trigger scale-ups).
Alex: Noted. We'll scope warmers to reserved capacity during deploy window to avoid autoscale noise. Thanks all.
